findings.text: Enabled Tasks Trace support provides reader entry and exit, asynchronous callback queuing, blocking grace wait, barrier, current grace expedite, and a completed batch query, all fronting one shared trace domain.
Disabled Tasks Trace builds provide trapping placeholders for callback queuing and reader entry and exit, signalling that the flavor is unavailable.
Sleepable RCU exposes normal index based reader entry and exit together with NMI safe entry and exit, untraced entry, and semaphore style down entry, with matching index based release paths.

Fast Sleepable RCU exposes counter handle based entry and exit for plain fast, fast updown, untraced fast, and down fast forms, with tiny builds encoding the index in the handle and tree builds using per CPU counter handles.
Tiny Sleepable RCU equates barrier with a blocking grace wait and treats expedite of the current grace as having no effect.
Sleepable RCU initialization covers generic and lockdep aware setup plus plain, fast and fast updown convenience forms, with conditional dependency map initialization and a header guard.
Protected pointer access offers a checked dereference plus plain and untraced conveniences, anchored by a helper that declares the required shared hold on a domain.
Lock dependency tracking for Sleepable RCU offers acquire, release and sync shims with an active implementation and an empty fallback.
Read flavor validation plus grace state queries provide completed state reporting and equality comparison over recorded states, with a fixed poll sizing constant.
Tiny and tree RCU expose full grace state helpers for equality, snapshot, poll start and poll check, conditional wait, and expedited variants, with tiny expedited service aliasing normal service.

Tiny RCU quiescence and lifecycle surface includes soft interrupt reporting, context switch reporting, CPU need and urgent quiescence hints, stall control, interrupt exit checks, task exit, deferred quiescence queries, boot end reporting, momentary and universal quiescence, and a header guard.
Tree RCU virtual context reporting and interrupt exit checks are minimal shims, and CPU hotplug hooks are null placeholders in both tiny and tree except for a no effect start report in tiny.
Single waiter support provides an initializer and init helper, an activity test, a publish current waiter helper, and blocking and timeout wait forms built over a shared wait core.
Sleepable reference counting provides biased initialization, current count reading, dead zone testing, acquisition, and two release forms for RCU safe context and for preemption controlled context.

Multi domain waiting offers a fan out core plus uninterruptible and state parameterized forms and a multi synchronize convenience, together with a conditional reschedule helper and a blocked reader test.

Full grace equality in tiny compares only the normal component while tree requires both normal and expedited components to match, and tiny sizes its full poll record for two entries while tree sizes for four.
Tiny expedited poll start and conditional wait alias their normal counterparts, tiny expedited full helpers forward through normal full state, and tiny expedited grace wait aliases normal grace wait.

Tasks Trace nesting keeps inner entries and exits as depth only updates while the outermost entry acquires a fast handle and the outermost exit publishes depth before releasing that handle, with ordering barriers around handle handoff.

Reference counts are stored biased down by one, reads add the bias back and report zero throughout the released to dead range, and dead testing accepts values at or above released but below the no reference marker.

Fast acquisition succeeds on the common path and defers to a slow path only on negative outcome, while release reports no completion on non negative outcome and defers otherwise, with saturation and dead bands absorbing transient drift.
Read flavor markers are distinct single bits, their union defines the all flavors set, and the slow grace set contains exactly the two fast flavors.

Tiny fast handles round trip between index and pointer representation, while tree fast entry samples the current counter pointer and tallies a lock count and tree fast exit tallies an unlock count with barriers separating the guarded region.

Single waiter blocking publishes the waiter before checking the condition, returns an interrupt error if a signal is pending in an interruptible state, and timeout forms skip waiting when the condition with timeout accounting already holds.

Multi waiting builds one callback entry and one synchronize record per requested domain and delegates to a shared fan out worker, with the multi synchronize form selecting tiny awareness and uninterruptible state.

Tiny lifecycle answers are fixed as no CPU need, no deferred quiescence, boot already ended, empty stall reset and momentary quiescence, barrier only universal quiescence, and a distant stall check delay.

Normal, fast, fast updown and NMI safe entries declare shared acquisition on a domain with flavor validation, while matching exits declare shared release with matching validation, and untraced and down forms preserve the hold without lock dependency interaction.
Active lock dependency shims forward acquire, release and sync to the dependency map while fallback builds expand to no effect, and domain initializers wire a per site key with optional map naming.

Checked dereference requires a shared hold on the named domain and evaluates either a caller condition or a held query, with plain form supplying a false condition and untraced form supplying a true condition.

Trace reader entry attempts dependency acquisition on the trace domain and trace reader exit always releases that dependency, even when nesting makes the underlying fast handle management unnecessary.

Internal release warns when invoked in preemptible context without an RCU read hold, the RCU safe release runs directly in caller context, and the generic release brackets the internal step with preemption control.
The blocking grace helper record holds a callback head for queuing, a completion for waking the waiter, and a saved grace sequence for debugging.
The single waiter record centers on a task pointer that starts cleared, is published to the current task when preparing to wait, and is tested for presence to report activity.
Trace reader state per task pairs a nesting depth with a saved fast counter handle, where depth distinguishes inner from outer transitions and the handle is only meaningful at depth zero boundaries.
Full grace records carry a normal sequence in all builds and an additional expedited sequence in tree builds, with helpers to snapshot, start polling and test completion through those components.

Sleepable RCU domains expose a dependency map for tracking and a current counter pointer for fast paths, counters expose separate lock and unlock tallies, and tiny builds treat the handle as an encoded index.
Reference records center on an atomic count with biased storage, where the stored zero denotes one live reference and higher bands denote saturation, release, death and absence.

Trace reader depth starts at zero, entry increments with outermost entry acquiring the fast handle, exit decrements with inner exits only storing depth and the final exit clearing depth before releasing the handle.

Reference state moves from biased init through increment and decrement, with non negative fast outcomes staying on the fast path and negative outcomes entering slow handling across saturation, released, dead and no reference bands.

Waiter progress publishes the waiter, sets the requested sleep state, checks the condition, honors pending signals with an interrupt result, invokes schedule or timeout schedule, and always finishes the waiter before returning.

Tree fast critical sections pair a lock tally at entry with an unlock tally at exit over the sampled counter, while tiny sections pair index acquisition with index derived release through pointer encoding.
Conditional grace waiting in tiny only declares sleepability without blocking, with full and expedited conditionals forwarding to the same declaration through their stored sequences.
Kernel boot completion and task exit provide no effect completion marking, a true ended query, and empty per task cleanup in tiny builds.
CPU lifecycle exposes prepare, online, offline, dead and dying hooks as null placeholders in tiny and partially in tree, with tiny start reporting as an empty action.

Quiescence entry covers soft interrupt and context switch reporting, virtual switch reporting, momentary and universal quiescence, stall reset, urgent hints and interrupt exit checks, with tree virtual reporting forwarding to context switch handling.
Disabled trace builds trap on callback queuing and on reader entry and exit, so callers must not invoke the trace flavor when it is compiled out.
Normal release warns on unexpected index bits, down forms warn when entered in NMI context, and fast forms warn when RCU is not watching, indicating misuse of the chosen flavor or context.
Tiny conditional wait and expedited wait do not actually wait, CPU need and deferred quiescence always report false, and blocked reader testing is only meaningful under preemptible RCU.
Tiny index to pointer conversion truncates through integer and boolean representation, so handles are only valid as opaque round trip values and must not be dereferenced as ordinary pointers.
Tree fast tallies select between per CPU increment and atomic increment depending on NMI safety need, so correctness depends on matching the configured counter update form on both entry and exit.
Untraced dereference unconditionally satisfies its extra check, and conditional rescheduling temporarily drops and retakes RCU read hold around scheduling in debug or non preemptible builds.
Reference zone markers are zero for one reference, 0x7FFFFFFF for maximum, 0xA0000000 for saturated, 0xC0000000 for released, 0xE0000000 for dead, and 0xFFFFFFFF for no reference.
Sleepable read flavors are 0x1 for normal, 0x2 for NMI, 0x4 for fast and 0x8 for fast updown, with the all set as their union and the slow grace set as fast plus fast updown.
Completed synchronize state is marker 0x1, same state comparison is equality over recorded values, completed query returns that marker, and active SRCU poll sizing is two.
Active full poll sizing is two in tiny builds and four in tree builds.
Header guards define standard include sentinels and CPU hotplug hooks are null placeholders as listed.
Single waiter initialization clears the task pointer, tiny stall recheck delay is a fixed multiple of the timer frequency, and trace batch completion query reports zero.
